rule: Second held-out set, written before any of these questions was run and after the fixes for the first set's failures were built. The platform must not be changed for any question here. Known overlaps: H2-C05 and H2-A02 are the same paper (nimodipine, SAH), as are H2-C08 and H2-A01 (furosemide before CRRT); populations such as acute respiratory failure and subarachnoid haemorrhage also appeared in the first set. All evidence is abstract-level.

items.question: In adults with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury who need CRRT, is furosemide given before CRRT associated with 28-day mortality?

items.likely_platform_difficulty: Opioid-equivalent conversion across drugs; time-varying exposure after ventilation; VAP by ICD code is unreliable; subgroup variables are comorbidities not sex/age

items.question: Does the association between the systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI) and mortality in type 2 diabetics with ischemic stroke act partly through blood glucose?
items.citation: Li Z, Liu Q, Feng Y. Blood glucose mediation of the association between SIRI and mortality in T2DM complicated with ischemic stroke. Sci Rep 2026;16(1):5785.
items.population_as_in_paper: 1,235 patients with type 2 diabetes and ischemic stroke, MIMIC-IV
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: SIRI (neutrophil x monocyte / lymphocyte); mediator blood glucose
items.design_as_in_paper: Retrospective cohort; Cox, restricted cubic spline, subgroup analyses, mediation analysis
items.main_results: SIRI HR 1.09 (1.07-1.12) for 28-day and 1.08 (1.06-1.10) for 1-year mortality; nonlinear (P<0.01); glucose mediated 13.72% of 28-day association (P<0.01); not significant for 1-year (P=0.17)
items.evidence_quality: Abstract-level via Europe PMC record; all numbers read from abstract; HR unit (per SIRI unit vs per SD) not stated
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Mediator measured at the same time as exposure (temporal order of SIRI vs glucose unclear); HR unit unknown; mediation-proportion method not named

items.question: Is furosemide given before continuous renal replacement therapy associated with lower 28-day mortality in sepsis-associated AKI, and does the effect differ by chronic kidney disease or dose?
items.citation: Shen SY, Fu L, Liang DY. Pre-CRRT furosemide and mortality in sepsis-associated AKI: a retrospective cohort study. PLoS One 2026;21(4):e0347094.
items.population_as_in_paper: 969 adults with sepsis-associated AKI who required CRRT, MIMIC-IV; 560 after 1:1 PSM
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: Furosemide within 72 h before CRRT start; high dose >90 mg/72 h
items.design_as_in_paper: Retrospective cohort; PSM, Cox, subgroup interaction, dose analysis
items.main_results: 28-day mortality 44.3% vs 58.6%, HR 0.58 (0.46-0.73); unmatched HR 0.59 (0.49-0.72); greater benefit without CKD (interaction p=0.021); high dose HR 0.62 (0.45-0.85); 7-day HR 0.45, 90-day 0.59, in-hospital 0.50
items.evidence_quality: Abstract-level via Europe PMC record; numbers read; effect modifier is CKD, not sex/age
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Cohort anchored on CRRT start (time-zero); exposure window of 72 h before CRRT; furosemide-after-CRRT immortal time; sepsis-AKI definition

items.question: Can in-hospital death in heart failure patients be predicted better by adding longitudinal chest X-rays to electronic health record data?
items.citation: Li D, Xing W, Zhao J, et al. Multimodal deep learning for predicting in-hospital mortality in heart failure patients using longitudinal chest X-rays and electronic health records. Int J Cardiovasc Imaging 2025;41(3):427-440.
items.population_as_in_paper: Heart failure patients in MIMIC-IV linked to MIMIC-CXR (n not read)
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: Longitudinal chest X-ray images plus structured EHR data (MN-STDT multimodal deep model, pre-trained on CheXpert)
items.design_as_in_paper: Deep-learning prediction model, SHAP interpretation
items.main_results: AUC-ROC 0.8620 multimodal; 0.8166 EHR only; 0.7479 chest X-ray only
items.evidence_quality: Abstract-level via Europe PMC record; AUCs read; cohort size not read
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Platform may be tempted to answer the EHR-only part (AUC 0.8166) and silently drop the image part
items.out_of_scope_reason: The key predictor is the chest X-ray image itself (deep learning on images); the platform has no image data, only structured tables. A structured-only version of the question would be in scope but is not what the paper asks.

items.question: Can large language models detect radiographic evidence of pneumonia from radiology reports?
items.citation: Chen W, Li X, Qu Z, et al. Large language models for pneumonia detection in radiology reports via text analysis. PLOS Digit Health 2026;5(9):e0001104.
items.population_as_in_paper: Radiology reports from MIMIC-IV, plus an independent tertiary-hospital dataset from Guangzhou (n not read)
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: Free-text radiology reports; LLMs (e.g. gemma3-27b) with and without retrieval-augmented generation
items.outcome_as_in_paper: Report-level pneumonia evidence (classification accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1)
items.design_as_in_paper: Inference-only LLM evaluation, 1,000 patient-level clustered bootstrap replicates
items.main_results: RAG generally improved performance; gemma3-27b accuracy 96.4% on MIMIC-IV, 87.6% on Guangzhou data
items.evidence_quality: Abstract-level via Europe PMC record; accuracy figures read; sample sizes not read
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Platform may substitute ICD-code pneumonia for the text task
items.out_of_scope_reason: The data are free-text radiology reports (NLP / language model evaluation), not structured tables; also uses a second hospital's data.

items.question: Can a reinforcement-learning policy set mechanical ventilator settings in ICU patients better than clinicians' recorded practice?
items.citation: Zhang B, Mi Y, Miao Y. Physics-informed Koopman-constrained implicit Q-learning for safe offline reinforcement learning in mechanical ventilation. Biomed Phys Eng Express 2026;12(3).
items.population_as_in_paper: 15,446 patients, 1.58 million hourly observations, MIMIC-IV
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: Hourly physiological state and ventilator-setting actions; offline RL (PIK-IQL) with respiratory-mechanics constraints
items.outcome_as_in_paper: Estimated policy value versus behaviour (clinician) policy; safety (aggressive actions)
items.design_as_in_paper: Offline reinforcement learning, off-policy evaluation, Rosenbaum sensitivity analysis
items.main_results: Policy value +0.088 over behaviour policy (95% CI 0.078-0.096); zero aggressive actions; critical Gamma* = 3.0
items.evidence_quality: Abstract-level via Europe PMC record; numbers read
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Platform may reduce it to an association of ventilator settings with outcome
items.out_of_scope_reason: The product is a learned treatment policy (recommendation of what to set) from reinforcement learning, a causal-policy claim, not an observational association.

items.question: Is selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) use before ICU admission associated with delirium in older patients with sepsis?
items.citation: Xu H, Su Y. Association between pre-ICU selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor use and delirium in older patients with sepsis: a study based on the MIMIC-IV database. Ann Pharmacother 2026.
items.population_as_in_paper: 11,768 older septic patients, MIMIC-IV; 754 used SSRIs before ICU admission
items.exposure_or_predictors_as_in_paper: SSRI use before ICU: no use, pre-ICU only, continuous; dose, drug type (e.g. citalopram)
items.design_as_in_paper: Retrospective cohort; multivariable logistic regression, subgroups, drug half-life sensitivity analyses
items.main_results: Pre-ICU SSRI OR 0.759 (0.637-0.901), P=0.002; continuous use during ICU P=0.493; medium dose OR 0.789 (0.639-0.972); citalopram OR 0.660 (0.495-0.874); no significant interactions
items.evidence_quality: Abstract-level via Europe PMC record; numbers read. Exact data source of 'pre-ICU' use (in-hospital orders before ICU vs outpatient/pre-admission) not stated in the abstract - verify in full text before use
items.likely_platform_difficulty: Platform may treat in-hospital pre-ICU prescriptions as the exposure and answer; the stop depends on whether the paper's exposure is pre-admission medication
items.out_of_scope_reason: Exposure is drug use before ICU admission (outpatient / pre-admission medication), which MIMIC-IV records only partly; the question is about use before the study window, not an in-hospital treatment. Caveat: exact source not confirmed.
